symptom: `mxcli report traceability --format json --junit junit.xml` produced output byte-identical to the run without --junit; each requirement's `tests` stayed a list of names, while `report tests --junit` on the same file showed 10 passed / 1 failed.
file: cmd/mxcli/projectreport/traceability.go TraceRequirement.TestResults / TraceTestResult / testsCell / testsClass. Test: cmd/mxcli/projectreport/traceability_junit_2340_test.go
cause: The traceability command did read the JUnit file into the evidence (CollectTests carries each TestInfo.Status), but CollectTraceability reduced each requirement's reaching tests to their names, so the results never reached the report.
insight: **A flag that is accepted, documented and plumbed can still be dropped at the last projection.** The evidence path was correct end to end up to `tr.Tests = append(tr.Tests, t.Name)`. The fix keeps `tests` (names) for existing readers and adds `testResults` [{name, status}] — 'not run' where no result was read — and the rendered table shows 'name (failed)' with the cell marked bad, so 'built, test failing' no longer reads as 'built and proven'.
